I guess I'll give some actionable fantasy advice re: De'Zhaun Stribling vs. Deebo Samuel (or any other WR3/WR4 type) instead of vague-posting polls.

I think it's pretty likely that Deebo sees the field more and therefore averages more FPG than Stribling, assuming everyone is healthy.

But the contingent potential for Stribling if/when the 49ers suffer injuries is high. And we just know less about him, making the upper-tail (90th+ percentile) outcome better than Deebo's.

What do you do with that? It depends on how big your starting lineup and bench are.

The deeper the lineups, the more likely that Deebo can actually help you in a FLEX spot from the jump.

The deeper the benches, the more likely you'll actually still have Stribling on your roster if/when he gets an opportunity.

IMO, there are a few WRs going around the top-100 on ESPN/Yahoo/Sleeper who have both a Week 1 role locked down and a strong upside outcome. All of them are written up in my draft guide/ranked inside my top-100, and I wouldn't take Stribling ahead of any of them.

But after that, in a shallow(er) league (start 2 WRs and 1 FLEX) with 6+ bench spots? Go for it. The vast majority of those players (especially WRs) won't matter anyway.

These preseason riser players are often very good picks in home leagues (i.e., what most people play in) and very bad picks in plugged-in/high-stakes/analyst leagues. The rankings I see several suggesting on here seem outlandish to me, but the reality is that many of you will get him much later in your actual leagues, against which I won't really argue.
